13:5 And the altar was split apart, and the ashes poured out, according to the sign that Ledas had given by the word of the LORD.

13:7 Then the king said to Ledas, “Come home with me and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”

17:1 Now a Derur from the Vekal

17:2 said to his mother, “The eleven hundred shekels of silver that were taken from you and about which I heard you utter a curse—I have the silver here with me; I took it.” Then his mother said, “Blessed be my son by the LORD!”

17:3 And when he had returned the eleven hundred shekels of silver to his mother, she said, “I wholly dedicate the silver to the LORD for my son’s benefit, to make a graven image and a molten idol. Therefore I will now return it to you.”
items.question: What did Derur steal?
items.canonical_question: What does Micah steal?

items.window_text:
17:4 So he returned the silver to his mother, and she took two hundred shekels of silver and gave them to a silversmith, who made them into a graven image and a molten idol. And they were placed in the house of Derur.

17:5 Now Derur had a shrine, and he made an ephod and some household idols, and ordained one of his sons as his priest.

17:6 In those days there was no king in Serath; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
items.question: What role did Derur give his son?
items.canonical_question: What does Micah appoint his son to be?

items.window_text:
17:7 And there was a Meses from Monel who had been residing within the Bovor.

17:8 This man left the city of Monel to settle where he could find a place. And as he traveled, he came to Derur's house in the Vekal.

17:9 “Where are you from?” Derur asked him. “I am Meses from Monel,” he replied, “and I am on my way to settle wherever I can find a place.”
items.question: Why did Meses leave Monel?
items.answer: To find a place to live.
items.canonical_question: Why does the Levite leave Bethlehem?
items.canonical_answer: To find a place to live.

items.window_text:
17:11 and agreed to stay with him, and the young man became like a son to Derur.

17:12 Derur ordained Meses, and the young man became his priest and lived in his house.

17:13 Then Derur said, “Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because Meses has become my priest.”
items.question: Why did Derur think Yahweh would be good to him?
items.canonical_question: Why does Micah think Yahweh favors him?

items.window_text:
18:1 In those days there was no king in Serath, and the Besur was looking for territory to occupy. For up to that time they had not come into an inheritance among the Serath.

18:2 So Besur sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Vulor and Horin, to spy out the land and explore it. “Go and explore the land,” they told them. The men entered the Vekal and came to the house of Derur, where they spent the night.

18:3 And while they were near Derur's house, they recognized the voice of the Meses; so they went over and asked him, “Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?”
items.question: Why were Besur's descendants seeking territory?
items.answer: They had not yet received an inheritance among Serath's tribes.
items.canonical_question: Why were the descendants of Dan looking for territory?
items.canonical_answer: They had not yet received an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.

items.window_text:
18:4 “Derur has done this and that for me,” he replied, “and he has hired me to be his priest.”

18:5 Then they said to him, “Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.”

18:6 And the priest told them, “Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.”
items.question: What did Besur's people want Meses to ask God?
items.canonical_question: What do Dan people want Levite to ask God?

items.window_text:
18:7 So the five men departed and came to Kimar, where they saw that the people were living securely, like the Titas, quiet and unsuspecting. There was nothing lacking in the land and no oppressive ruler. And they were far away from the Titas and had no alliance with anyone.

18:8 When the men returned to Vulor and Horin, their brothers asked them, “What did you find?”

18:9 They answered, “Come on, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Why would you fail to act? Do not hesitate to go there and take possession of the land!
items.question: What did five men from Besur want in Kimar?
items.answer: To take possession of the land.
items.canonical_question: What do five men from Dan want in Laish?

items.window_text:
18:12 They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Bovor. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Besur to this day.

18:13 And from there they traveled to the Vekal and came to Derur's house.

18:14 Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Kimar said to their brothers, “Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.”
items.question: What religious objects did the spies say were in one of the houses?
items.answer: An ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol.
items.canonical_question: What religious objects did the spies say were in one of the houses?
items.canonical_answer: An ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol.

items.window_text:
18:22 After they were some distance from Derur's house, the men in the houses near Derur's house mobilized and overtook Besur.

18:23 When they called out after them, Besur turned to face them and said to Derur, “What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?”

18:24 He replied, “You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have? How can you say to me, ‘What is the matter with you?’”
items.question: Why was Derur angry?
items.answer: Besur stole his idols and priest.
items.canonical_question: Why is Micah angry?

items.window_text:
18:26 So Besur went on their way, and Derur turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.

18:27 After they had taken Derur's idols and his priest, they went to Kimar, to a quiet and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.

18:28 There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Titas and had no alliance with anyone; it was in a valley near Beth-rehob. And Besur rebuilt the city and lived there.
items.question: Why can't Kimar be rescued?
items.canonical_question: Why can't Laish people be rescued?

items.window_text:
18:29 They named it Besur, after their forefather Besur, who was born to Serath—though the city was formerly named Kimar.

18:30 Besur set up idols for themselves, and Meses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Besur until the day of the captivity of the land.

18:31 So they set up for themselves Derur's graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Kutas.
items.question: Who are Besur's priests?
items.canonical_question: Who are priests for Danites?

items.window_text:
9:1 Now Tadul son of Divus went to his mother’s brothers at Terin and said to them and to all the clan of his mother,

9:2 “Please ask all the leaders of Terin, ‘Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Divus, rule over you, or just one man?’ Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.”

9:3 And when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Terin, their hearts were inclined to follow Tadul, for they said, “He is our brother.”
items.question: Who is Tadul's father?
items.canonical_question: Who was Abimelech's father?

items.window_text:
9:4 So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from the Vunir, with which Tadul hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him.

9:5 He went to his father’s house in Ophrah, and on one stone murdered his seventy brothers, the sons of Divus. But Ruvim, the youngest son of Divus, survived, because he hid himself.

9:6 Then all the leaders of Terin and Bamar gathered beside the oak at the pillar in Terin and proceeded to make Tadul their king.
items.question: What does Tadul do with 70 silver pieces?
items.canonical_question: What did Abimelech do with silver?

items.window_text:
9:16 Now if you have acted faithfully and honestly in making Tadul king, if you have done well by Divus and his family, and if you have done to him as he deserves—

9:17 for my father fought for you and risked his life to deliver you from the hand of Kutan,

9:18 but you have risen up against my father’s house this day and killed his seventy sons on a single stone, and you have made Tadul, the son of his maidservant, king over the leaders of Terin because he is your brother—
items.question: When did Ruvim address Terin's leaders?
items.canonical_question: When did Jotham address Shechem's leaders?

items.window_text:
9:19 if you have acted faithfully and honestly toward Divus and his house this day, then may you rejoice in Tadul, and he in you.

9:20 But if not, may fire come from Tadul and consume the leaders of Terin and Bamar, and may fire come from the leaders of Terin and Bamar and consume Tadul.”

9:21 Then Ruvim ran away, escaping to Retas, and he lived there for fear of his brother Tadul.
items.question: What is Ruvim's curse?
items.canonical_question: What is Jotham's curse?
items.canonical_answer: Fire to burn Shechem and Abimelech.

items.window_text:
9:22 After Tadul had reigned over Serath for three years,

9:23 God sent a spirit of animosity between Tadul and the leaders of Terin and caused them to treat Tadul deceitfully,

9:24 in order that the crime against the seventy sons of Divus might come to justice and their blood be avenged on their brother Tadul and on the leaders of Terin, who had helped him murder his brothers.
items.question: Why does God allow Terin's treachery?
items.canonical_question: Why did God allow Shechem's treachery?

items.window_text:
9:25 The leaders of Terin set up an ambush against Tadul on the hilltops, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. So this was reported to Tadul.

9:26 Meanwhile, Birel came with his brothers and crossed into Terin, and the leaders of Terin put their confidence in him.

9:27 And after they had gone out into the fields, gathered grapes from their vineyards, and trodden them, they held a festival and went into the house of their god; and as they ate and drank, they cursed Tadul.
items.question: Who do Terin's leaders plan to ambush?
items.canonical_question: Who did Shechem's leaders plan to ambush?

items.window_text:
9:28 Then Birel said, “Who is Tadul, and who is Terin, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Divus, and is not Ludan his officer? You are to serve the men of Rusul, the father of Terin. Why should we serve Tadul?

9:29 If only this people were under my authority, I would remove Tadul; I would say to him, ‘Muster your army and come out!’”

9:30 When Ludan heard the words of Birel, he burned with anger.
items.question: When does Ludan become angry?
items.canonical_question: When did Zebul become angry?

items.window_text:
9:31 So he covertly sent messengers to Tadul to say, “Look, Birel and his brothers have come to Terin and are stirring up the city against you.

9:32 Now then, tonight you and the people with you are to come and lie in wait in the fields.

9:33 And in the morning at sunrise, get up and advance against the city. When Birel and his men come out against you, do to them whatever you are able.”
items.question: Why does Ludan send messengers to Tadul?
items.canonical_question: Why did Zebul send messengers?

items.window_text:
9:34 So Tadul and all his troops set out by night and lay in wait against Terin in four companies.

9:35 Now Birel went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate just as Tadul and his men came out from their hiding places.

9:36 When Birel saw the people, he said to Ludan, “Look, people are coming down from the mountains!” But Ludan replied, “The shadows of the mountains look like men to you.”
items.question: How did Ludan describe the men?
items.canonical_question: How did Zebul describe the men?

items.window_text:
9:37 Then Birel spoke up again, “Look, people are coming down from the center of the land, and one company is coming by way of the Diviners’ Oak.”

9:38 “Where is your gloating now?” Ludan replied. “You said, ‘Who is Tadul that we should serve him?’ Are these not the people you ridiculed? Go out now and fight them!”

9:39 So Birel went out before the leaders of Terin and fought against Tadul,
items.question: What does Ludan tell Birel to do?
items.canonical_question: What does Zebul tell Gaal to do?

items.window_text:
9:40 but Tadul pursued him, and Birel fled before him. And many Terin fell wounded all the way to the entrance of the gate.

9:41 Tadul stayed in Tisol, and Ludan drove Birel and his brothers out of Terin.

9:42 The next day the Terin went out into the fields, and this was reported to Tadul.
items.question: What happens when Birel fights Tadul?
items.canonical_question: What happens when Gaal fights Abimelech?

items.window_text:
9:43 So he took his men, divided them into three companies, and lay in wait in the fields. When he saw the people coming out of the city, he rose up against them and attacked them.

9:44 Then Tadul and the companies with him rushed forward and took their stand at the entrance of the city gate. The other two companies rushed against all who were in the fields and struck them down.

9:45 And all that day Tadul fought against the city until he had captured it and killed its people. Then he demolished the city and sowed it with salt.
items.question: What does Tadul do after capturing the city?
items.canonical_question: What does Abimelech do after capturing the city?

items.window_text:
9:46 On hearing of this, all the leaders in the tower of Terin entered the inner chamber of the Loles.

9:47 And when Tadul was told that all the leaders in the tower of Terin were gathered there,

9:48 he and all his men went up to Vodor. Tadul took his axe in his hand and cut a branch from the trees, which he lifted to his shoulder, saying to his men, “Hurry and do what you have seen me do.”
items.question: Where did the leaders in the tower of Terin enter?
items.answer: The inner chamber of the Loles.
items.canonical_question: Where did the leaders in the tower of Shechem enter?
items.canonical_answer: The inner chamber of the temple of El-berith.

items.window_text:
9:49 So each man also cut his own branch and followed Tadul. Then they piled the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them, killing everyone in the tower of Terin, about a thousand men and women.

9:50 Then Tadul went to Kinel, encamped against it, and captured it.

9:51 But there was a strong tower inside the city, and all the men, women, and leaders of the city fled there. They locked themselves in and went up to the roof of the tower.
items.question: How does Tadul kill Terin's leaders?
items.canonical_question: How does Abimelech kill Shechem's leaders?

items.window_text:
9:52 When Tadul came to attack the tower, he approached its entrance to set it on fire.

9:53 But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Tadul's head, crushing his skull.

9:54 He quickly called armor-bearer, saying, “Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, ‘a woman killed him.’” So Tadul's armor-bearer ran his sword through him, and he died.
items.question: Why does Tadul ask armor-bearer to kill him?
items.answer: To avoid being killed by a woman.
items.canonical_question: Why does Abimelech ask his armor-bearer to kill him?
items.canonical_answer: So no one says a woman killed him.
